metaDescription: Robot vacuum mops whose docks wash and dry the mop for you: how roller, pad and arm designs differ, what upkeep remains, and six picks ranked.
expertTake: The eufy C28 is the pick for scrubbing, since its roller mop is rinsed constantly while it works and dried afterward. The Lefant M210 OMNI is the value choice, with a self-cleaning and self-drying base at the lowest tier here. If your floors are mostly carpet or unsealed wood, skip the category: a mop dock adds upkeep you will never use.
introParagraphs: A self-cleaning mop robot is really two machines in one: a vacuum that picks up dry debris and a floor washer that must not smear its own dirty water around. The dock is what separates the good ones from the rest, because it washes the mop, and in better models dries it too.

What you are paying for is time. The question to ask of any candidate is how much of the washing, refilling and drying it really does without you, and what chores the listing quietly leaves behind. Six machines are sorted here on exactly that basis.

products.name: eufy C28 15,000Pa Vacuum With HydroJet Roller Mop
products.description:
The C28 is built around a mop that behaves like a tool instead of a rag. A 28cm roller with 24 water ports spins at 270 RPM and is fed fresh water as it turns, so the surface that touches the floor is clean at every pass. That is a mechanical difference from pad systems that simply drag a damp cloth.

On the dry side, a DuoSpiral brush is rated for hair as long as 30 centimetres, which speaks to the homes with long-haired residents and pets. Next to the Roomba 505X it trades a pad system and a famous name for a harder-working roller, and next to the Roborock Qrevo S5V it gives up the extending edge arm in exchange for more scrubbing action.

Remove the roller monthly, rinse the shaft and check the end caps for wrapped thread. Empty the dirty tank after each run even if the dock does it, because a tank left standing overnight is where odor starts.
products.bestFor: Sticky kitchens and long-haired households that want a roller that really scrubs.
pros: 28cm roller with 24 ports keeps the contact surface clean
270 RPM spin lifts dried spots instead of smearing
DuoSpiral brush handles hair up to 30 cm
Dock washes the roller between runs
cons: Roller needs rinsing and drying care to avoid mildew
No edge-extending arm like the Roborock models

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S5V 12,000Pa FlexiArm Vacuum and Mop
products.description:
What sets the Qrevo S5V apart is how it treats the edge of a room. The FlexiArm mop swings out to reach baseboards and corners, which is where a round mop pad leaves a stripe of grime. The dock then dries the pad with warm air, which closes the loop on the self-cleaning idea and tackles the sour smell of a damp pad.

It carries a rubberized floating main brush as part of a certified zero-tangle system, and obstacle handling is part of the package. Compared with the eufy C28 it has a lower suction rating at 12,000Pa and a pad-style mop, so it fits better when edge coverage matters more than stain scrubbing.

Wash the dock tray regularly and replace pads before they wear flat. Check the arm joint for hair, and wipe the avoidance sensors with a dry cloth.
products.bestFor: Homes with lots of baseboard, cabinet edges and corners to mop.
pros: FlexiArm reaches corners a round pad misses
Warm-air drying in the dock fights odor
Floating rubber brush with zero-tangle design
Brushless motor with 12,000Pa headline
cons: Pad mop is gentler on dried-on spills than a roller
Dock needs a clear footprint and regular tray cleaning

products.name: Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro 20,000Pa FlexiArm Vacuum and Mop

specList.label: Edge system
specList.value: FlexiArm extends to edges and corners

products.description:
The Qrevo 2 Pro is the same idea as the S5V with the numbers turned up: 20,000Pa against 12,000Pa and a dual zero-tangle system aimed squarely at pet households. FlexiArm still extends to edges and corners, so it keeps the Roborock strength for baseboards.

The step up from the S5V is the motor and the 2026 refresh of the dock features, not a different mopping principle. That means the decision is about carpets and pet hair, where the higher figure and tangle system help, versus a tidy hard-floor home where the S5V is already enough. The Shark NeverTouch Pro below is the rival for people who prefer a bigger self-emptying promise.

Expect to refill clean water and empty the dirty tank, and to replace the mop and dust bag on schedule. Rinse the dock tray weekly and check the zero-tangle rollers for hair at their ends.
products.bestFor: Pet owners who want Roborock's arm reach and the stronger motor.
pros: FlexiArm mop reaches edges and corners
Dual zero-tangle system suits pet hair
20,000Pa gives headroom on carpet
Self-cleaning multifunction dock
cons: Costs more than the S5V for the same mop principle
Suction number overstates real carpet gains

products.name: Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro Self-Refill Mop Combo
products.description:
The NeverTouch Pro attacks the three chores that remain on most mop docks: emptying, refilling and pad care. It dumps debris into a bin rated for 60 days, refills its own water, and washes and dries the pad. The name suggests you never touch it, and the listing backs that with up to a month of hands-free cleaning.

Five PowerDetect technologies target hidden debris, and NeverStuck lifts the robot over obstacles and onto rugs, which the listing says doubles coverage in some homes. Compared with the Roomba 505X it offers a refill system as well as a washing one, so it asks less of you, and compared with the eufy C28 it uses a pad rather than a roller.

Because the dock does so much, the dock is what to maintain: clean the wash tray and check the water lines for scale if your water is hard. Replace pads and the bag on schedule.
products.bestFor: Owners who want the dock to handle emptying, refilling and pad care.
pros: Dock empties, refills and washes in one routine
60-day bin capacity for dirt
NeverStuck lifts the robot over obstacles
Pad is washed and dried automatically
cons: Pad mop is lighter than a roller on stuck-on spills
Dock has more parts that can scale or clog

products.name: Lefant M210 OMNI 20,000Pa Self-Cleaning Base Mop
products.description:
The M210 OMNI proves a self-cleaning dock does not need a flagship price. A real-time fresh-water cleaning system rinses the mop as it works, and the base station cleans and dries it afterward. At 85mm tall and 280mm across it is also compact enough to slip under low furniture.

The 20,000Pa claim matches the Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro on paper, though with the budget tier you should expect plainer mapping and a lighter dock. Against the Shark NeverTouch Pro it lacks the self-refill step, so you will fill a tank yourself, but it costs much less.

Watch the base station's tray and tank, and replace the mop and bag as they wear. Because it is a lower-cost machine, keep the sensors clean and avoid cluttered floors where its simple avoidance could stall it.
products.bestFor: Small and mid-size homes that want a self-cleaning dock at a lower tier.
pros: Self-cleaning and self-drying base at a lower tier
Only 85mm tall for low furniture
Real-time fresh water rinsing while mopping
Tangle-free roller for pet hair
cons: No self-refill, so you fill the tank
Simpler sensors than the premium Roborock and Shark docks

products.name: iRobot Roomba 505X Vacuum and Mop With AutoWash Dock
products.description:
The Roomba 505X makes sense when long-term support matters more than the strongest scrubber. Its AutoWash dock empties debris for up to 75 days, then washes and refreshes the pads, which covers the self-cleaning brief in full. PerfectEdge works on the wall line.

Its DualClean pads are a gentler tool than the eufy C28's roller, so very sticky floors need more passes, and the 70x suction claim compares against older Roombas. The reason to buy is the parts and service network, which matters in year four when a pad or a bag needs replacing.

Rinse the dock tray every week, let the pads air-dry between runs, and keep spare bags. If a pad starts to smell even after washing, replace it rather than trying to rescue it, since fibre that has gone sour will keep spreading odor over the floor. Place the dock on level hard floor to keep the return clean.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prioritise parts availability and a long bin interval.
pros: Dock washes and refreshes pads after each run
Up to 75 days between bin emptyings
PerfectEdge targets the wall-floor seam
Wide parts and service availability
cons: Pads scrub less than a roller on dried spills
Suction claim compares with older Roombas only

buyingCriteria.explanation: Self-cleaning can mean as little as rinsing the mop, or as much as emptying, refilling, washing and drying. The Shark NeverTouch Pro lists all four, the Roomba 505X covers emptying and washing, and the Lefant M210 OMNI cleans and dries. Count which chores you still do before comparing prices.

A roller like the 28cm unit on the eufy C28 presses and wipes with a clean surface throughout, which beats a pad on dried food. A pad like the Roomba's DualClean is lighter work and lasts longer between swaps. Choose the roller for kitchens and the pad for gentle daily upkeep.

A damp mop left in a closed dock turns sour within days. Warm-air drying, as on the Roborock Qrevo S5V, or hot-air drying on the eufy family, removes that smell. A dock with no drying stage leaves you to air the pad yourself.

Round robots cannot reach square corners, so edge design matters. The Roborock FlexiArm extends outward and PerfectEdge on the Roomba widens pad coverage by a stated 18 percent in the Roomba range. Choose arm designs if your home is full of cabinets and baseboards.

Mop docks are for sealed hard floors. Carpet needs a lift or a pad that detaches, and unfinished wood should never get a wet mop. If more than a third of your floor is carpet, a vacuum-only robot is the better buy.

Self-refill docks like the Shark NeverTouch Pro draw from a tank and can scale in hard water. Descale on the maker's schedule and use filtered water if you can. A scaled line is the usual reason a dock stops refilling.

specDecoder.meaning: The roller's rotation speed sets how hard it scrubs the floor. Higher RPM with fresh water lifts dried residue.
specDecoder.watchFor: The eufy C28 lists 270 RPM, which no pad-based machine in this lineup matches.

specDecoder.meaning: A peak motor figure rather than the pickup you get on the floor. It matters most on carpet.
specDecoder.watchFor: Qrevo 2 Pro and M210 OMNI both list 20,000Pa, but the docks differ far more than the motors.

specDecoder.meaning: Days of light use before the dock bin fills. Pets and carpet shorten it substantially.
specDecoder.watchFor: Shark lists 60 days and Roomba 505X up to 75 days.

specDecoder.meaning: A swinging arm that extends the mop to edges and corners. It reaches where a fixed round pad cannot.
specDecoder.watchFor: It appears on the Qrevo S5V and Qrevo 2 Pro, and adds a moving part to check.

specDecoder.meaning: A lifting feature that helps the robot climb obstacles and thresholds. It lowers the number of rescues.
specDecoder.watchFor: Shark lists it on the NeverTouch Pro, which is relevant on rug-heavy floors.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored each dock by how many chores it removes: emptying, refilling, washing and drying. The Shark NeverTouch Pro covers all four and the Roomba 505X two or three. A dock that leaves the pad damp lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: Rollers, pads and arms were compared on how they treat dried messes and edges. The eufy C28 roller at 270 RPM and the Roborock FlexiArm sit at opposite ends. We favored the mechanism that solves a real floor problem.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair and brush design
howWeEvaluated.description: Zero-tangle systems on the Roborock pair and the DuoSpiral brush on the eufy were judged from stated mechanisms and owner feedback patterns. A mop robot that jams its brush cannot clean a floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep after year one
howWeEvaluated.description: Pads, rollers, bags and descaling were counted as continuing work. The Lefant M210 OMNI and Roomba 505X have simple lists, while the self-refill dock adds scale control. We favored the shortest honest list.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value by tier
howWeEvaluated.description: Relative tiers run from the Lefant M210 OMNI at the lowest to the Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro and Shark NeverTouch Pro at the top. A higher tier had to remove a chore or add reach, not only a bigger suction figure.

rows: Support network and long bin interval

Strongest motor or most automated dock

cards.label: Roller mops
cards.text: The eufy C28 and Lefant M210 OMNI present a clean roller to the floor continuously. They lift dried spots better and are easier to keep fresh. They need the roller rinsed and dried carefully.

cards.label: Pad mops
cards.text: The Roomba 505X, Roborock Qrevo S5V and Shark NeverTouch Pro use pads that are washed in the dock. They are gentler and suit daily upkeep. Stubborn spots need extra passes.

howToChoose.note: Roller for messy kitchens, pad for tidy daily maintenance.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A zero-tangle brush, a dirty-water tank that is easy to rinse, and a dock that dries the mop. Pet urine accidents are the reason to keep wet mode away from carpet. Plan on weekly tray cleaning.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro and eufy C28 are the best fit. The eufy suits long-haired pets with its 30 cm hair rating, and the Roborock adds edge reach.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want the dock to remove every chore or your home has many edges. The Shark NeverTouch Pro and Roborock Qrevo models spend money on automation and reach.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your floors are small and mostly clean. The Lefant M210 OMNI gives a self-cleaning dock without the premium.

maintenance.task: Rinse the wash tray and dirty tank
maintenance.why: Film builds in the tray and causes odor. A quick rinse and wipe prevents it.

maintenance.task: Take out and rinse the roller or pad
maintenance.why: Grit trapped in a worn mop scratches finished floors. Replace when it flattens.

maintenance.interval: As the maker advises, more often in hard water
maintenance.why: Scale blocks refill and wash nozzles. Use filtered water where you can.

maintenance.task: Replace the dust bag or empty the bin
maintenance.why: A full bag weakens vacuuming even though the mop still works.

maintenance.task: Wipe sensors and the dock contacts
maintenance.why: Dust confuses avoidance and charging. Use a dry microfiber cloth.

faq.q: What does self-cleaning mean on a robot mop?
faq.a: The dock washes the mop, and in better models also dries it. Some docks go further and empty the dust bin and refill the water tank. Check the listing to see which of these chores a given model really handles.

faq.q: Is a roller mop better than a pad?
faq.a: For dried spills, yes, because a roller presents a clean surface continuously. Pads are gentler and suit light daily upkeep. The eufy C28 and Roomba 505X show the two approaches.
No. They are meant for sealed hard floors, and they must lift or avoid carpet. Keep wet mode off rugs and unfinished wood.

faq.q: Do I still need to do anything?
faq.a: Yes. You will refill clean water on most docks, empty the dirty tank, and replace bags and pads. The Shark NeverTouch Pro reduces this the most.

faq.q: Will hard water damage the dock?
faq.a: Scale can clog nozzles and lines over time. Descale on the maker's schedule or use filtered water to keep the dock running.

faq.q: Is it worth buying a premium model?
faq.a: Only if the extra buys a chore removed or an edge reached. The Qrevo 2 Pro's higher suction matters mostly on carpet, while the S5V's arm and drying matter on hard floor.
